written.myAnswer: Almost all an atom’s mass is in its nucleus because the nucleus contains protons and neutrons, while electrons have very little mass.
Elements differ because their atoms have different numbers of protons in the nucleus.
Tritium is radioactive because its nucleus is unstable.
An atom absorbs energy when an electron moves to a higher energy level and emits energy when an electron moves to a lower energy level.
The second shell is farther from the nucleus than the first shell, so an electron in it has greater energy.
The gas pressure is lowered to reduce collisions between gas particles, allowing charged particles to move through the tube.

Classically, an electron was pictured as a particle moving around the nucleus in a definite path. Later, its wave-like nature was recognised; its exact position and path cannot be specified in that way.
Radioactive nuclei are unstable because their neutron-to-proton ratio is unbalanced; they emit radiation to become more stable.

Cathode rays had the same properties regardless of the gas or electrode material, showing that electrons are present in all elements. Positive-ray properties depend on the gas; hydrogen positive rays revealed the proton.
An ordinary hydrogen atom has a nucleus containing one proton and one electron outside the nucleus; its nucleus contains no neutron.
Radiation from a radioactive isotope can transfer enough energy to atoms to remove electrons. The atoms become positive ions, and the removed electrons are free electrons.
Radioactivity is the spontaneous emission of radiation from unstable nuclei. Radioactive isotopes are used in medicine, to date organic remains, and as tracers in industry or agriculture.
Normalising the listed abundances gives a relative atomic mass of approximately 200.642, or 200.64 (no unit).
Scientists can synthesise elements by bombarding atomic nuclei with high-energy particles, causing nuclear reactions that produce new elements.
The nucleus can be compared with the Sun and electrons with planets, but the comparison is limited: electrons show wave-like behaviour and do not simply travel in fixed planetary paths.
